pillarForecast.why: A 1.5s pulsing arrow plus the 380px minimum removes the run-33 death; like other fixes it will mostly be absorbed silently, at most a passing 'saw it coming'. Residual risk: a pursuer entering inside the lane where a death wall is on screen still reads as close.

pillarForecast.pillar: Reference moment 2 (rocks as a toolkit, chasers are the star)
pillarForecast.why: Rocks are cut to 65% (A) and ~34% (B) of v8's count, so fewer pursuers die and there is less nearby to lure into; in B this can repeat run 32's 'tried to but they never came'. Chasers will be on screen a lot (good), but with fewer tools.
Bigger rocks are easier targets to steer a pursuer into and easier to see; outsmarting chasers stays the high point, especially in A.
Thrusters unchanged; expect silence, and 'skill issue' self-blame when he clips a big rock.
Every run still starts at sector 1; a bit easier than v8, so he may reach Crossfire or Rams, but six runs of the same opening sectors invites mild sameness late in the session.

biggestRisk: Too few rocks, not too small ones: with fewer asteroids, fewer pursuers die, so up to 3-4 chasers pile up on him with nothing close to lure them into. In B (2-3 rocks on screen) this repeats run 32's 'I should have gone for the asteroids… they never came', and he ends up trying to outrun faster pursuers, which he can't. He'll likely blame himself at first, then ask for more asteroids (a middle count) once he senses it.
abVerdict: He likely won't name A vs B as a variant difference (about 60%), but the first run (B) is where he notices 'big asteroids' and likes them. A should feel better in play (more rocks to use, more lure kills, his 'better's and 'satisfying'/'clever' tags fall on A runs); sector reached will be roughly equal. If he states a preference it's for A, or a third option: 'big like these, but more of them'.
